question.text: What is the solution to the following system of inequalities? \[ \begin{cases} n+2 < 5 \\[5pt] 1-2n \leq 3 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of $n$ that satisfy both $n+2 < 5$ and $1-2n \leq 3$ simultaneously.

  • First, we solve $n+2 < 5 \,\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} n+2 & < 5 \\[5pt] n+2-2 & < 5 -2 \\[5pt] n &< 3 \end{align*}

\[ \]

  • Then, we solve $1-2n \leq 3 \,\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 1-2n & \leq 3 \\[5pt] 1-2n -1 & \leq 3 -1\\[5pt] -2n & \leq 2 \\[5pt] (-1)\cdot(-2n) & \geq (-1)\cdot 2 \\[5pt] 2n & \geq -2\\[5pt] \dfrac{2n}{2} & \geq \dfrac{-2}{2} \\[5pt] n & \geq -1 \end{align*}

To find the values of $n$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

\[\]

Thus, the final solution is $n\in [-1,3).$

question.text: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $1 \lt 2x-1 \leq 5$ and $1-2x \leq 3.$
question.explanation:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection.

  • First, we solve $1 \lt 2x-1 \leq 5 \,\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 1 &\lt 2x-1 \leq 5 \\[5pt] 1 +1 &\lt 2x-1+1 \leq 5+1 \\[5pt] 2 &\lt 2x \leq 6 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{2} &\lt \dfrac{2x}{2} \leq \dfrac{6}{2} \\[5pt] 1 &\lt x \leq 3 \end{align*}
  • Then, we solve $1-2x \leq 3 \,\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 1-2x & \leq 3 \\[5pt] 1-2x-1 & \leq 3-1 \\[5pt] -2x & \leq 2 \\[5pt] (-1) \cdot (-2x) & \geq (-1)\cdot 2 \\[5pt] 2x & \geq -2 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2x}{2} &\geq \dfrac{-2}{2} \\[5pt] x &\geq -1 \end{align*}

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

\[\]

Thus, the final solution is $x \in (1,3].$

question.text:
What is the solution to the following system of inequalities?
\[
\begin{cases}
	y-5 \leq 2 \\[3pt]
	2y+7 > 11
\end{cases}
\]
question.explanation:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of $y$ that satisfy both $y-5 \leq 2$ and $2y+7 > 11$ simultaneously.

  • First, we solve $y-5 \leq 2 \,\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} y-5 &\leq 2\\[5pt] y-5+5 &\leq 2+5\\[5pt] y &\leq 7 \end{align*}

\[ \]

  • Then, we solve $2y+7 > 11 \,\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 2y+7 &> 11\\[5pt] 2y+7-7 &> 11-7\\[5pt] 2y &> 4\\[5pt] \dfrac{2y}2 &> \dfrac{4}2 \\[5pt] y &> 2 \end{align*}

\[\]

To find the values of $y$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

\[\]

Thus, the final solution is $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{<} y \leq\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{7}.$
